strings.app.subtitle: Network diagnostics
strings.top.trace.title: Traceroute
strings.top.ping.title: Ping Monitor
strings.top.ping.sub: Periodic probes (ICMP / TCP) · latency, success and loss rate
strings.top.http.title: HTTP Monitor
strings.top.http.sub: Periodic URL checks · status code, response time, content match and certificate
strings.top.settings.title: Settings
strings.top.about.title: About
strings.trace.desc: Probe hops with ICMP (Windows: IcmpSendEcho; Linux/macOS: native ICMP sockets, falling back to system ping). MTR is on by default: discover the path, then probe each hop on an interval. Annotate with qqwry.ipdb, GeoIP, and ASN.
strings.trace.label: Target
strings.trace.empty: No data · enter a target and click Start Trace
strings.ping.host_ph: Host or IP; add a port for TCP: host:443 / [v6]:443
strings.ping.empty: List empty · add hosts then click Start Monitor
strings.alias.title: Edit Alias
strings.alias.desc: Set a display alias for this target.
strings.detail.title: Ping Details
strings.import.title: Batch Import
strings.import.desc: One target per line. Optional alias after a comma: host,alias. host:port or [IPv6]:port uses TCP ping. Blank lines and lines starting with # are ignored.
strings.import.placeholder:
One host per line, optional alias after a comma, # starts a comment, e.g.
1.1.1.1,Cloudflare
8.8.8.8
2001:4860:4860::8888,Google DNS
strings.import.conflict.title: Alias Conflicts
strings.import.conflict.desc: These hosts already exist with a different alias. Replace all, or skip all?
strings.dup.title: Replace Alias?
strings.dup.desc: Host “{0}” already exists with alias “{1}”. Replace with “{2}”?
strings.settings.data_desc: Download data files yourself and set paths below. Location/region/ASN show “—” when missing.
strings.settings.startup_desc: Opens the Ping Monitor page by default. Choose whether Ping monitoring, HTTP monitoring and Traceroute tabs start automatically at launch; unticked ones stay stopped until you start them.
strings.settings.language_desc: Built-in and custom language packs. Changes apply immediately.
strings.settings.language_browser: Stored in this browser only; guests can set it too. Choose Follow default to use the default language.
strings.settings.language_default_desc: Saved in the config file; used by the desktop app and by every browser without its own language.
strings.settings.theme_desc: Light, dark, or follow the system appearance. Applies immediately.
strings.settings.flags_desc: Region column prefers embedded flagcdn 16×12 PNGs; falls back to flag emoji (Segoe UI Emoji) when missing.
strings.settings.config_desc: Ping list, interval, language, theme and data paths are saved at:
strings.settings.lang_packs: Custom language packs: put *.json in {0} or a lang folder next to the exe.
strings.about.name: HinaTracer
strings.about.desc: A native mygo UI network diagnostics tool: ICMP traceroute with MTR and multi-tab support, Ping monitoring, IP lookup, with qqwry.ipdb, GeoIP and ASN data for location, region flags and autonomous systems. One-click data file download in Settings. Supports IPv4 / IPv6.
strings.settings.asn_desc: iptoasn.com ip2asn-combined (ASN number, org name, registered country; IPv4/IPv6; .tsv or .tsv.gz)
strings.top.lookup.title: IP Lookup
strings.lookup.title: Query
strings.lookup.desc: Enter an IP (v4/v6) or domain, one per line. With a port (host:port / [v6]:port) latency is a TCP connect, otherwise one ICMP echo. Domains resolve to all A/AAAA addresses.
strings.lookup.placeholder:
One IP or domain per line, e.g.
1.1.1.1
example.com
2606:4700:4700::1111
strings.lookup.status.empty: Enter at least one IP or domain
strings.settings.dl_all.title: Download / update data files
strings.settings.dl_all.desc: Downloads qqwry.ipdb, Country.mmdb and ip2asn-combined.tsv.gz. Overwrites configured paths, or saves into the config directory and fills empty paths. Uses system proxy (HTTP(S)_PROXY). On Windows, Go reads proxy from environment variables only.
strings.update.status.saved: Package saved to {0}; please install it manually
strings.update.err.ratelimit: GitHub API rate limit reached; please try again later
strings.update.err.manual: This installation cannot update itself; please open the download page
strings.update.err.server: Server mode never installs updates itself; upgrade with your package manager (e.g. apt install ./HinaTracer-…-server.deb)
strings.update.title: New version v{0} available
strings.update.settings.title: Updates
strings.update.settings.desc: Check GitHub Releases for new versions.
strings.top.webui.title: WebUI
strings.top.webui.sub: Use every feature in a browser · settings shared with the desktop app
strings.web.status.title: Web server
strings.web.desc: Once started, Ping monitoring, traceroute, IP lookup, data downloads and settings are available in a browser. The web page and the desktop window share the same settings and running tasks, so a change in one shows up in the other right away.
strings.web.err.need_password: Set an access password before listening on a non-local address
strings.web.err.pw_short: Password must be at least 6 characters
strings.web.msg.pw_saved: Access password saved; open pages must sign in again
strings.web.listen.title: Listen address
strings.web.listen.host_desc: 127.0.0.1: this computer only. 0.0.0.0: other devices on your network too (password required)
strings.web.warn.exposed: Other devices can reach this address; they must sign in with the access password
strings.web.warn.need_password: This address is open to other devices: set an access password below first, or the server will not start
strings.web.autostart: Start the web server when HinaTracer opens
strings.web.pw.title: Access password
strings.web.pw.desc: When set, the web page asks for this password first. Only a salted hash is stored, never the password itself.
strings.web.cli.title: Run without a window
strings.web.cli.desc: You can also run only the web server, without a window (e.g. on a server or an always-on PC). See --help for all options:
strings.web.table_hint: Click headers to sort · Ctrl/Shift to multi-select · double-click for details · right-click for more
strings.web.theme_desc: The web page follows the system light/dark appearance by default
strings.web.settings.title: WebUI
strings.web.settings.desc: Change the listen address and access password on the WebUI page of the desktop app.
strings.web.update.headless: Updates cannot be installed in no-window mode; please open the download page
strings.chart.title: Latency trend
strings.http.batch.title: Batch add URLs
strings.http.batch.desc: One URL per line, optionally followed by a space and an alias; lines starting with # are ignored.
strings.http.empty: No HTTP targets yet. Enter a URL above to add one.
strings.reset.confirm.title: Permanently clear saved statistics?
strings.reset.confirm.desc: Saving history to disk is on: resetting permanently clears the saved cumulative statistics (counts, success and failure rates, latencies) of {0} target(s). They will not come back after a restart, and this cannot be undone.
strings.reset.confirm.required: Saving history to disk is on: resetting permanently clears the saved statistics of {0} target(s). Pass confirm (CLI: --yes) to proceed.
strings.http.edit.title: Edit HTTP target
strings.http.body_hint: A body is sent only with POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE and custom methods. With Content-Type empty, a body starting with { or [ is sent as application/json, anything else as text/plain.
strings.http.match_hint: Plain text by default (case-sensitive). Tick “Regular expression” to use a Go regular expression; tick “Invert” to fail when it is found.
strings.ph.http.custom_method: Method name in capitals, e.g. PROPFIND
strings.ph.http.match: Text the body must contain; with regex ticked, a pattern such as "status":\s*"ok"
strings.ph.http.headers: One per line, e.g. Authorization: Bearer xxx
strings.ph.http.batch:
One URL per line, optionally followed by a space and an alias, e.g.
https://example.com/health Website
https://api.example.com/status API
# lines starting with # are ignored
strings.ph.remote.password: Admin password of the remote WebUI (not saved)
strings.http.detail.title: HTTP target details
strings.remote.title: Data source
strings.remote.desc: Local: monitoring runs on this computer. Remote WebUI: this window becomes a client of another HinaTracer WebUI; local monitoring and the local WebUI stop.
strings.remote.password_note: The password is only used to obtain an API token and is never stored.
strings.remote.token_keep: Leave empty to keep the saved token
strings.remote.guest_note: Connects as a guest; every page is read-only.
strings.remote.err.auth: Authentication failed: wrong password or token, or guest access is off.
strings.remote.webui_off: The local WebUI is off while using a remote data source (this window shows the remote server's data). The remote server's own WebUI is configured under Settings → Remote server settings; switch back to local in Settings → Data source to use the local WebUI.
strings.remote.autoconnect: Connect to the remote WebUI automatically at startup
strings.remote.autoconnect_desc: When on, the app starts in remote mode and connects with the saved token; if that fails it shows the status and keeps retrying, and you can switch back to local at any time.
strings.settings.scope.intro: Using a remote data source: settings marked "Local" only affect this computer; settings marked "Remote" are written to the remote server.
strings.settings.scope.inactive_group: Local (takes effect when you switch back to the local data source)
strings.settings.local_webui.title: Local WebUI
strings.settings.local_webui.desc: The local WebUI does not run while using a remote data source; switch back to local to start and configure it on the WebUI page.
strings.settings.alerts.title: Desktop alerts
strings.settings.alerts.desc: This computer only; all off by default. A target counts as down after {0} failures in a row (used by notifications and the tray tooltip).
strings.settings.alerts.threshold: Failures in a row before a target counts as down
strings.settings.alerts.notify: Send a system notification when a target goes down or recovers
strings.settings.alerts.close_to_tray: Minimize to tray when closing the window
strings.remote.server.title: Remote server settings
strings.remote.server.desc: These settings are saved on the remote server, the same as its WebUI settings page.
strings.remote.server.listen_note: The listen address takes effect the next time the remote server starts its WebUI.
strings.history.export.title: Export latency history
strings.settings.history.title: Monitoring history
strings.settings.history.desc: Covers Ping and HTTP monitoring history and statistics. When off, only recent data is kept in memory; when on, it is saved to {0} and older data is rolled up per minute/hour.
strings.web.guest.desc: When on, the login page shows “Sign in as guest”. Guests need no password and can only view: they cannot change anything and do not see file paths or access settings. Requires an access password.
strings.web.guest.need_password: Set an access password before turning on guest mode
strings.web.guest.tip: You are browsing as a guest: view only, no changes.
strings.web.token.title: API tokens
strings.web.token.desc: For MCP (AI clients) and the command-line client. Admin tokens can view and change, guest tokens can only view. A token is shown only once, when it is created.
strings.web.token.name: Name
strings.web.token.created: Token “{0}” created. Copy it now; it cannot be shown again:
strings.web.token.once: Save this token now; it will not be shown again.
strings.web.token.err.name: Enter a token name
strings.web.token.err.role: Role must be admin or guest
strings.web.mcp.title: MCP (AI clients)
strings.web.mcp.desc: While the WebUI runs, MCP-capable AI clients can query and control HinaTracer at the address below. Enter it in the client and add the header Authorization: Bearer <API token>.
strings.web.mcp.stopped: Available once the WebUI is running
strings.web.listen.next_start: Saved; used the next time the WebUI starts
strings.web.listen.active_differs: Currently listening on {0} (differs from the saved setting {1}, e.g. set by a startup option)
strings.web.listen.saved_differs: Saved setting: {0} (used at the next start)
